title: The Death of the Author
text:
Structuralist criticism holds that meaning arises not from an author's intentions but from the differences between signs within a language system. Consequently, a literary text is treated as a network of relations rather than a vessel of private experience. Critics such as Roland Barthes went further, proclaiming the 'death of the author' and relocating interpretive authority to the reader. Such a shift, however, has been contested by those who argue that it dissolves the historical specificity of texts.

Opponents of this position maintain that a text cannot be divorced from the circumstances of its composition, and that biographical and historical evidence remains indispensable. Their objection is not merely methodological; it reflects a conviction that interpretation must answer to something beyond the reader's own invention. Yet the structuralist legacy persists, subtly shaping even those who reject its premises. Few contemporary critics, therefore, approach a novel as an unmediated window onto its creator's mind.

questions.text: According to the passage, where does structuralist criticism locate meaning?
options: In the differences between signs within a language system
In the historical period in which a text was written
In the emotional response of the reader

questions.text: What do opponents of the structuralist position maintain?
options: A text is entirely independent of its historical setting
A text cannot be separated from the circumstances of its composition
Biographical evidence should be dismissed altogether
Interpretation is purely a matter of the reader's invention

questions.text: What can be inferred about Roland Barthes's view of the reader's role in interpretation?
options: He considered the reader's role in interpretation central
He believed readers should defer to the author's biography
He rejected the idea that readers can interpret texts at all
He argued that texts have no interpretive value

questions.text: Why does the passage suggest that the influence of structuralism is still felt today?
options: Its premises shape even critics who oppose them
Its methods were officially adopted by every university
Its opponents have fully abandoned their objections
Biographical criticism has been completely discredited

paragraph_translations: Yapısalcı eleştiri, anlamın yazarın niyetlerinden değil, bir dil sistemi içindeki göstergeler arasındaki farklılıklardan doğduğunu savunur. Sonuç olarak, edebi bir metin özel deneyimin bir kabı olmaktan çok, ilişkiler ağı olarak ele alınır. Roland Barthes gibi eleştirmenler bir adım daha ileri giderek 'yazarın ölümü'nü ilan etmiş ve yorumlama yetkisini okura aktarmıştır. Ancak bu değişim, metinlerin tarihsel özgüllüğünü ortadan kaldırdığını savunanlar tarafından tartışmalı bulunmuştur.

Bu görüşün karşıtları, bir metnin yazıldığı koşullardan koparılamayacağını ve biyografik ile tarihsel kanıtların hâlâ vazgeçilmez olduğunu ileri sürer. Onların itirazı yalnızca yöntemsel değildir; yorumun okurun kendi icadının ötesindeki bir şeye hesap vermesi gerektiği inancını yansıtır. Yine de yapısalcılığın mirası sürmekte ve bu ilkeleri reddedenleri bile ince biçimde şekillendirmektedir. Bu nedenle günümüzde pek az çağdaş eleştirmen, bir romana yazarın zihnine aracısız bir pencere olarak yaklaşır.
